os_version: Windows 11 Pro 26100, 1920x1080 @ 100% (96 DPI), French locale, live in-use machine
app: Date and Time dialog (timedate.cpl) — legacy Win32/GDI dialog with a custom-drawn analog clock

stack_detection.signature: classic #32770 dialog class; UIA answers through the MSAA/Win32 proxy providers with a 25-node tree on first query

channel_setup: UI Automation via Python `uiautomation`; the pre-XAML dialog is served by UIA's built-in Win32/MSAA proxy providers. No flags, no permissions.

t1_read_text.detail: Date ('samedi 15 août 2026'), time ('14:07:08'), timezone string and the full DST explanation paragraph all read as exact strings (ValuePattern on edits + Name on texts).

t2_enumerate.detail: 6 buttons, 3 tabs (with selection state), 1 checkbox (toggle state), 3 value-bearing edits — all present with boxes; screenshot cross-check matches. One honest gap: the UAC shield glyph on 'Changer la date et l'heure...' (the needs-elevation affordance) is carried only by pixels; the channel does not represent it.

t3_live_value.detail: Not run — the only editable values here are the SYSTEM date/time; changing them is destructive and behind UAC. Live-value already proven on Notepad/Calculator.

t4_living_screen.detail: Both clocks tick in-channel every second: the custom-drawn ANALOG clock declares the digital time as its accessible Name (pane '14:07:09' -> '14:07:10' ...), and the Heure edit updates in lockstep. 6/6 polls saw the change. Changed-line cost 80 B (~20 tok) per tick vs 299 tok for a re-screenshot (~15x). Polling caveat kept honest: at 1 Hz with 36-269 ms capture latency the loop skipped one second (…13 -> …15); a production router should subscribe to UIA PropertyChanged events instead of polling.

t5_blind_action.detail: Deliberately not run: every actionable control in this dialog either changes system time settings or is behind UAC — outside the action allowlist. Blind action already proven on Calculator/Notepad.

t6_pictorial.detail: The custom-drawn analog clock face — the pictorial suspect — is NOT silent: its node carries the semantic value ('14:07:08') as the accessible name. 1990s-era Win32 accessibility annotation doing exactly what the thesis wants.

measurements.notes: View 280 tok ~ screenshot 299 tok (small dense dialog — near break-even, consistent with the density law). The living-screen economics are the point: 80 B of changed lines per second vs 299 tok/s of re-screenshots. diff_bytes_per_interaction=594 is the full unified-diff envelope per tick (context lines included); the semantic payload is the 80 B. Capture 37-269 ms (Win32 proxy jitter under load). No idle measurement: this dialog is never idle (clock always ticks) — idle=0 established on Notepad/Calculator cells.

runtime_verification.method: screenshot taken right after first distillation; every view line located in the image, values compared
runtime_verification.agreement: full agreement incl. the analog-clock name matching the painted clock hands' time; one pixels-only semantic found (UAC shield glyph), noted in t2
